  changes:
    # Every pull request of a repository with a Dockerfile builds its image:
    # the Dockerfile is the agents' own, so no list here could name its
    # inputs.
    runs-on: pr-untrusted
    outputs:
      build: ${{ steps.select.outputs.build }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: is there an image to build
        id: select
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          base=${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          git fetch -q origin "$base"
          if [ -f Dockerfile ]; then
            echo "build image: true"
            echo "build=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0
          fi
          if git cat-file -e "$(git merge-base "$base" HEAD):Dockerfile" 2>/dev/null; then echo "Dockerfile was deleted"; exit 1; fi
          echo "no Dockerfile: no image"
          echo "build=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  image:
    # Builds only, never pushes. Forgejo hands a job to a runner before its
    # `if` is evaluated, so the label carries the same test: with nothing to
    # build, an ordinary runner skips the job and no build VM is made.
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.build == 'true'
    runs-on: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.build == 'true' && 'pr-untrusted-build' || 'pr-untrusted' }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: wait for the build VM's buildkitd
        run: |
          set -u
          echo "buildkitd at $BUILDKIT_HOST, mTLS, server name $BUILDKIT_TLS_SERVERNAME"
          deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + 180 ))
          until buildctl --tlsdir "$BUILDKIT_TLS_DIR" --tlsservername "$BUILDKIT_TLS_SERVERNAME" debug workers; do
            if [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$deadline" ]; then echo "buildkitd did not answer within 3 minutes"; exit 1; fi
            sleep 3
          done
      - name: build the image
        run: |
          buildctl --tlsdir "$BUILDKIT_TLS_DIR" --tlsservername "$BUILDKIT_TLS_SERVERNAME" \
            build --progress=plain --frontend dockerfile.v0 --local context=. --local dockerfile=. \
            --output type=oci,dest=/dev/null

+// Package store is the app's storage contract: the API handlers and the
+// feature cards talk to a Store, never to a database driver. The SQLite
+// implementation lives in internal/sqlite.
+package store
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"errors"
+	"time"
+)
+
+// ErrNotFound is what every read answers for a row that is not there: an
+// email no account has, a session cookie no one holds, a slug no link owns.
+var ErrNotFound = errors.New("store: not found")
+
+// ErrDuplicate is what CreateUser answers for an email that already has an
+// account and CreateLink for a slug that is already taken.
+var ErrDuplicate = errors.New("store: already exists")
+
+// User is an account. PasswordHash is the bcrypt hash of the password and
+// must never leave the API.
+type User struct {
+	ID           int64
+	Email        string
+	PasswordHash string
+	CreatedAt    time.Time
+}
+
+// Session is a login: Cookie is the random value of the HttpOnly cookie,
+// ExpiresAt when it stops being valid.
+type Session struct {
+	Cookie    string
+	UserID    int64
+	ExpiresAt time.Time
+}
+
+// Link is a shortened URL owned by a user. Slug is unique. TotalClicks is
+// all the clicks ever recorded for it.
+type Link struct {
+	ID          int64
+	UserID      int64
+	Slug        string
+	TargetURL   string
+	CreatedAt   time.Time

+	Close() error

+// Package store is the app's storage contract: the API handlers and the
+// feature cards talk to a Store, never to a database driver. The SQLite
+// implementation lives in internal/sqlite.
+package store
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"errors"
+	"time"
+)
+
+// ErrNotFound is what every read answers for a row that is not there: an
+// email no account has, a session cookie no one holds, a slug no link owns.
+var ErrNotFound = errors.New("store: not found")
+
+// ErrDuplicate is what CreateUser answers for an email that already has an
+// account and CreateLink for a slug that is already taken.
+var ErrDuplicate = errors.New("store: already exists")
+
+// User is an account. PasswordHash is the bcrypt hash of the password and
+// must never leave the API.

+	ID           int64
+	Email        string
+	PasswordHash string
+	CreatedAt    time.Time
+}
+
+// Session is a login: Cookie is the random value of the HttpOnly cookie,
+// ExpiresAt when it stops being valid.

+	Cookie    string

+

+-- The app's schema: accounts, sessions, links and the clicks per UTC day.
+
+CREATE TABLE users (
+    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
+    email         TEXT    NOT NULL,
+    password_hash TEXT    NOT NULL,

+    email_lc      TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE GENERATED ALWAYS AS (lower(email)) STORED

+
+CREATE TABLE sessions (
+    cookie     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
+    user_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+    expires_at TEXT    NOT NULL
+);
+
+CREATE INDEX sessions_user_idx ON sessions (user_id);
+
+CREATE TABLE links (
+    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
+    user_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+    slug        TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
+    target_url  TEXT    NOT NULL,
+    created_at  TEXT    NOT NULL,
+    total_clicks INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
+);
+
+CREATE INDEX links_user_idx ON links (user_id);
+
+CREATE TABLE clicks (
+    link_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES links (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
+    day     TEXT    NOT NULL,
+    clicks  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
+    PRIMARY KEY (link_id, day)
+);

diff --git a/internal/server/session.go b/internal/server/session.go
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..8ae7680
--- /dev/null
+++ b/internal/server/session.go
@@ -0,0 +1,109 @@
+package server
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"crypto/rand"
+	"encoding/base64"
+	"errors"
+	"log"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"git.aisoftwarefactory.world/linkshort2/linkshort2/internal/store"
+)
+
+// SessionCookie is the name of the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie that
+// carries a login.
+const SessionCookie = "session"
+
+// sessionKey is what userContext keys the request by.
+type sessionKey struct{}
+
+// UserFrom reports the user the request's session cookie names, as the
+// session middleware put it on the request. Handlers of the API under
+// /api/ call it; an anonymous request has neither.
+func UserFrom(ctx context.Context) (*store.User, bool) {
+	u, ok := ctx.Value(sessionKey{}).(*store.User)
+	return u, ok
+}
+
+// session authenticates a request from its session cookie: it reads the
+// cookie, asks the store for the session and the user, and puts the user
+// on the request. A request without the cookie, or with one the store does
+// not know, reaches next unnamed; the handler answers 401 when it needs a
+// user. The cookie path is "/", so the browser sends it to every path.
+func (s *Server) session(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
+	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+		c, err := r.Cookie(SessionCookie)
+		if err != nil || c.Value == "" {
+			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
+			return
+		}
+		sess, err := s.store.GetSession(r.Context(), c.Value)
+		if err != nil {
+			if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+				logError(r.Context(), "session", err)
+			}
+			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
+			return
+		}
+		user, err := s.store.GetUserByID(r.Context(), sess.UserID)
+		if err != nil {
+			if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+				logError(r.Context(), "session user", err)
+			}
+			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
+			return
+		}
+		next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(context.WithValue(r.Context(), sessionKey{}, user)))
+	})
+}
+
+// newSessionCookie returns a random cookie value: 32 bytes, URL-safe base
+// 64 without padding.
+func newSessionCookie() (string, error) {
+	var b [32]byte
+	if _, err := rand.Read(b[:]); err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	return base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(b[:]), nil
+}
+
+// setSessionCookie puts the login cookie on the response: HttpOnly, so no
+// script reads it, SameSite=Lax, so it travels on a top-level GET (the
+// redirect of /<slug>) but not on another site's POST, and Secure only
+// over https.
+func setSessionCookie(w http.ResponseWriter, value string, expiresAt time.Time, secure bool) {
+	http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{
+		Name:     SessionCookie,
+		Value:    value,
+		Path:     "/",
+		Expires:  expiresAt.UTC(),
+		HttpOnly: true,
+		SameSite: http.SameSiteLaxMode,
+		Secure:   secure,
+	})
+}
+
+// clearSessionCookie drops the login cookie from the browser.
+func clearSessionCookie(w http.ResponseWriter, secure bool) {
+	http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{
+		Name:     SessionCookie,
+		Value:    "",
+		Path:     "/",
+		MaxAge:   -1,
+		HttpOnly: true,
+		SameSite: http.SameSiteLaxMode,
+		Secure:   secure,
+	})
+}
+
+// requestIsSecure reports whether the request came over https, directly or
+// behind a proxy that set X-Forwarded-Proto.
+func requestIsSecure(r *http.Request) bool {
+	if r.TLS != nil {
+		return true
+	}
+	return strings.EqualFold(r.Header.Get("X-Forwarded-Proto"), "https")
+}

+package server
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"crypto/rand"
+	"encoding/base64"
+	"errors"
+	"log"
+	"net/http"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	"git.aisoftwarefactory.world/linkshort2/linkshort2/internal/store"
+)
+
+// SessionCookie is the name of the HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie that
+// carries a login.
+const SessionCookie = "session"
+
+// sessionKey is what userContext keys the request by.
+type sessionKey struct{}
+
+// UserFrom reports the user the request's session cookie names, as the
+// session middleware put it on the request. Handlers of the API under
+// /api/ call it; an anonymous request has neither.
+func UserFrom(ctx context.Context) (*store.User, bool) {
+	u, ok := ctx.Value(sessionKey{}).(*store.User)
+	return u, ok
+}
+
+// session authenticates a request from its session cookie: it reads the
+// cookie, asks the store for the session and the user, and puts the user
+// on the request. A request without the cookie, or with one the store does
+// not know, reaches next unnamed; the handler answers 401 when it needs a
+// user. The cookie path is "/", so the browser sends it to every path.
+func (s *Server) session(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
+	return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
+		c, err := r.Cookie(SessionCookie)
+		if err != nil || c.Value == "" {
+			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
+			return
+		}
+		sess, err := s.store.GetSession(r.Context(), c.Value)
+		if err != nil {
+			if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+				logError(r.Context(), "session", err)
+			}
+			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
+			return
+		}
+		user, err := s.store.GetUserByID(r.Context(), sess.UserID)
+		if err != nil {
+			if !errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) {
+				logError(r.Context(), "session user", err)
+			}
+			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
+			return
+		}
+		next.ServeHTTP(w, r.WithContext(context.WithValue(r.Context(), sessionKey{}, user)))
+	})
+}
+
+// newSessionCookie returns a random cookie value: 32 bytes, URL-safe base
+// 64 without padding.
+func newSessionCookie() (string, error) {
+	var b [32]byte
+	if _, err := rand.Read(b[:]); err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	return base64.RawURLEncoding.EncodeToString(b[:]), nil
+}
+
+// setSessionCookie puts the login cookie on the response: HttpOnly, so no
+// script reads it, SameSite=Lax, so it travels on a top-level GET (the
+// redirect of /<slug>) but not on another site's POST, and Secure only
+// over https.
+func setSessionCookie(w http.ResponseWriter, value string, expiresAt time.Time, secure bool) {
+	http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{
+		Name:     SessionCookie,
+		Value:    value,
+		Path:     "/",
+		Expires:  expiresAt.UTC(),
+		HttpOnly: true,
+		SameSite: http.SameSiteLaxMode,
+		Secure:   secure,
+	})
+}
+
+// clearSessionCookie drops the login cookie from the browser.
+func clearSessionCookie(w http.ResponseWriter, secure bool) {
+	http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{
+		Name:     SessionCookie,
+		Value:    "",
+		Path:     "/",
+		MaxAge:   -1,
+		HttpOnly: true,
+		SameSite: http.SameSiteLaxMode,
+		Secure:   secure,
+	})
+}
+
+// logError records a failure the handler cannot answer to the client. The
+// message is only about the app's own fault: never a cookie, an email or a
+// password, which would land in the logs.
+func logError(ctx context.Context, what string, err error) {
+	_ = ctx
+	log.Printf("server: %s: %v", what, err)
+}
+
+// requestIsSecure reports whether the request came over https, directly or
+// behind a proxy that set X-Forwarded-Proto.
+func requestIsSecure(r *http.Request) bool {
+	if r.TLS != nil {
+		return true
+	}
+	return strings.EqualFold(r.Header.Get("X-Forwarded-Proto"), "https")
+}

kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: linkshort2
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: linkshort2
spec:
  # One replica with Recreate: a rolling update would stall on the second
  # pod's attach of the ReadWriteOnce data volume.
  replicas: 1
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: linkshort2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: linkshort2
    spec:
      # registration's pull secret in every environment's namespace
      imagePullSecrets:
        - name: forgejo-registry
      # the namespace enforces Pod Security "restricted": without these
      # fields no pod is admitted
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 65532
        runAsGroup: 65532
        fsGroup: 65532
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: linkshort2
          # the environment's kustomization pins the digest CI built
          image: git.aisoftwarefactory.world/linkshort2/linkshort2
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            capabilities:
              drop:
                - ALL
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          env:
            - name: DATA_DIR
              value: /data
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 20
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
              memory: 64Mi
            limits:
              memory: 256Mi
      volumes:
        - name: data
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: data
        - name: tmp
          emptyDir: {}

detail.text:
Foundation card done. Summary of what I built:

- **`internal/store`** — `store.Store` interface (CreateUser, GetUserByEmail/ByID, CreateSession, GetSession, DeleteSession, CreateLink, GetLinkBySlug, ListLinksByUser, DeleteLink, RecordClick, GetClickStats) with sentinels `ErrNotFound`, `ErrDuplicate`, `ErrInvalid`.
- **`internal/sqlite`** — SQLite implementation on `modernc.org/sqlite` v1.57.0 (pure Go), single writer connection, WAL/FK pragmas, embedded migrations under `internal/sqlite/migrations/20261001004336_init.sql` applied in name order and remembered in `schema_migrations`.
- **`internal/server`** — session middleware (`session` cookie → store → user on the context, `UserFrom`, `requireUser`, HttpOnly/SameSite=Lax/Secure cookie helpers) and `New` wiring the store from `DataDir` (or an injected `Config.Store`) plus a stub `POST /api/signup` and `GET /api/me` so the contract runs end to end.
- Tests: `TestHealthz` (the acceptance item), signup→healthz end-to-end, session-middleware tests, and a full store-contract test against SQLite.

Note for reviewers: the migration lives at `internal/sqlite/migrations/` because `//go:embed` cannot reach a directory outside its package; CI's timestamp naming rule still applies.

`bash check` is green (npm lint/test/build, go vet, gofmt, gosec, `go test -race`). I recommend merging: it establishes the contracts every later card imports, adds no breaking change, and keeps the template's checks intact.
